newsitem.title: USA: BPA says 500 KV Ore. line restart still uncertain.
newsitem.headline: BPA says 500 KV Ore. line restart still uncertain.

text.p: A restart time for a key 500 kilovolt (KV) segment of the Pacific Intertie power transmission system linking the Northwest to southern California remains uncertain, a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) spokesman said Monday.
"We are working at getting the line up. It appears to be crucial to raising the Intertie rating," the spokesman added.
On Friday, the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) approved increasing the Intertie capacity to 6,250 megawatts (MW) from the current limit of 5,200 MW.
Work on the 500 KV John Day-Slatt line in Oregon was halted last Wednesday when a crane flipped because of the muddy, rainy weather conditions.
BPA is still assessing the line's status, a process hampered by the fact that the work is being done by a contractor, the BPA spokesman said.
"There are concerns over whether a road needs to be built in order to accomodate the crane," he noted.
But he said current moderate weather conditions may help speed the process.
Meanwhile, the study group convened by the WSCC still needs to review Intertie operating procedures before the lines can be re-energized.
A conference call to address those procedures will be held Tuesday, the BPA spokesman said.
